source.text: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out from there the Jesus withdrew into the districts of Tyre and Sidon.

en.L: And going out from there, Jesus withdrew into the districts of Tyre and Sidon.
en.B: Jesus left that place and went away to the region around Tyre and Sidon.
en.R: Jesus left that place and went to the area near the cities of Tyre and Sidon.

es.L: Y saliendo de allí, Jesús se retiró a las regiones de Tiro y Sidón.
es.B: Jesús salió de aquel lugar y se fue a la región de Tiro y Sidón.
es.R: Jesús salió de aquel lugar y fue a la zona cercana a las ciudades de Tiro y Sidón.

fr.L: Et sortant de là, Jésus se retira dans la région de Tyr et de Sidon.
fr.B: Jésus partit de là et se retira dans la région de Tyr et de Sidon.
fr.R: Jésus a quitté cet endroit. Il est allé dans la région proche des villes de Tyr et de Sidon.

sw.L: Na alipotoka huko, Yesu alijitenga kwenda pande za Tiro na Sidoni.
sw.B: Yesu aliondoka mahali pale, akaenda katika eneo la Tiro na Sidoni.
sw.R: Yesu aliondoka pale, akaenda sehemu iliyo karibu na miji ya Tiro na Sidoni.

decisions.choice: Tyre and Sidon: Gentile cities on the coast north of Galilee
decisions.reason: The two cities were in Phoenicia. Jesus named them in 11:21-22 as Gentile towns that would have repented.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away, as after opposition before
decisions.reason: Matthew uses the verb when Jesus moves away after conflict (12:15; 14:13).

decisions.choice: into the districts: to the area of Tyre and Sidon, perhaps only near the border
decisions.reason: The woman "came out from those regions" (15:22), which may mean that Jesus stayed near the border. Matthew does not say exactly where he was.

decisions.choice: the cities of
decisions.reason: Readable says that these are cities.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal (15:33 "disent", 15:34 "dit")
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ Χαναναία ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων ἐκείνων ἐξελθοῦσα ἔκραζεν λέγουσα· Ἐλέησόν με, κύριε υἱὸς Δαυίδ· ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, a woman Canaanite from the regions those having come out was crying out saying, Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; the daughter of me badly is demon-possessed.

en.L: And look, a Canaanite woman from those regions came out and was crying out, saying, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is severely demon-possessed."
en.B: A Canaanite woman who lived in that region came out and kept calling out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! A demon has my daughter in its grip, and she suffers terribly."
en.R: A woman from that area came to Jesus. She was a Canaanite, not a Jew. She kept shouting, "Lord, Son of David, please have pity on me! My daughter has a demon, and it is hurting her terribly."

es.L: Y mira, una mujer cananea, que había salido de aquellos territorios, gritaba diciendo: «¡Ten compasión de mí, Señor, Hijo de David! Mi hija está gravemente endemoniada».
es.B: Una mujer cananea que vivía en aquella región salió y se puso a gritar sin parar: «¡Señor, Hijo de David, ten compasión de mí! Un demonio tiene atrapada a mi hija, y ella sufre terriblemente».
es.R: Una mujer de aquella zona se acercó a Jesús. Era cananea, no judía. Gritaba una y otra vez: «¡Señor, Hijo de David, ten piedad de mí, por favor! Mi hija tiene un demonio, y la hace sufrir muchísimo».

fr.L: Et voici, une femme cananéenne, sortie de ces territoires, criait, disant : « Aie pitié de moi, Seigneur, Fils de David ! Ma fille est cruellement tourmentée par un démon. »
fr.B: Une femme cananéenne qui vivait dans cette région sortit et se mit à crier : « Seigneur, Fils de David, aie pitié de moi ! Un démon tient ma fille, et elle souffre terriblement. »
fr.R: Une femme de cette région est venue vers Jésus. C’était une Cananéenne : elle n’était pas juive. Elle n’arrêtait pas de crier : « Seigneur, Fils de David, s’il te plaît, aie pitié de moi ! Ma fille a un démon, et il lui fait terriblement mal. »

sw.L: Na tazama, mwanamke mmoja Mkanaani, aliyetoka katika maeneo yale, alikuwa akilia kwa sauti, akisema, "Nihurumie, Bwana, Mwana wa Daudi! Binti yangu anasumbuliwa vibaya na pepo."
sw.B: Mwanamke Mkanaani aliyeishi katika eneo lile alikuja, akaendelea kulia kwa sauti, "Bwana, Mwana wa Daudi, nihurumie! Pepo amemshika binti yangu, naye anateseka sana."
sw.R: Mwanamke mmoja wa eneo lile alimjia Yesu. Alikuwa Mkanaani, si Myahudi. Aliendelea kupiga kelele, "Bwana, Mwana wa Daudi, tafadhali nionee huruma! Binti yangu ana pepo, na pepo huyo anamtesa vibaya sana."

decisions.choice: Canaanite: a Gentile of that region, called by the ancient name of Israel's neighbors
alternatives: a descendant of the Canaanites only
decisions.reason: The Canaanites were the peoples of the land before Israel. Mark 7:26 calls her a Syrophoenician by birth. Matthew's older name sets her among Israel's ancient neighbors.

decisions.choice: Son of David: the title of the promised king
decisions.reason: As in 9:27, the title names Jesus as the Messiah. A Gentile woman uses Israel's own title for him.

decisions.choice: Lord: a respectful address, and in Matthew more than that
decisions.reason: As in 8:2, those who come in faith call Jesus "Lord". She uses the word three times (15:22, 25, 27).

decisions.choice: was crying out: she kept calling
decisions.reason: The tense shows she went on calling, as the disciples complain in 15:23.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: not a Jew
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name meant for the story.

decisions.choice: Señor, with a capital
decisions.reason: The woman uses the polite address that also means "Lord", and in Matthew it says more than politeness (meaning decision m3). As the English "Lord", Spanish writes "Señor" with a capital, here and in verses 25 and 27.

decisions.choice: Seigneur
decisions.reason: As in Mark 7:28: the style guide gives "Monsieur" where the word is only polite and "Seigneur" for those who turn to Jesus in faith. She calls him Son of David, kneels and pleads (m3), and Jesus praises her faith in 15:28, so "Seigneur" at every level, also in 15:25 and 15:27.

decisions.choice: Bwana, with a capital
decisions.reason: Swahili uses one word for "sir" and "Lord". The woman's address says more than politeness in Matthew (meaning decision m3), so it is written "Bwana", as the English "Lord", here and in verses 25 and 27.

source.text: ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῇ λόγον.

records.literal_gloss: He but not answered her a word.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not answer her a word.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave her no answer, not even a word.
en.R: But Jesus did not say anything to her.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no le contestó ni una palabra.
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no le dio ninguna respuesta, ni una sola palabra.
es.R: Pero Jesús no le dijo nada.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne lui répondit pas un mot.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne lui fit aucune réponse, pas même un mot.
fr.R: Mais Jésus ne lui a rien dit.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakumjibu neno lolote.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakumpa jibu lolote, hata neno moja.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu hakumwambia chochote.

decisions.choice: did not answer her a word: complete silence
decisions.reason: Matthew says that Jesus was silent but not why. His words in 15:24 explain the limit he felt bound by.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἠρώτουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἀπόλυσον αὐτήν, ὅτι κράζει ὄπισθεν ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And having come the disciples of him were urging him saying, Send away her, because she cries out after us.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came and were urging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us."
en.B: His disciples came and kept pressing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Send her away, because she keeps shouting behind us."
en.R: His followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Send her away! She keeps following us and shouting."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos se acercaron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} insistían, diciendo: «Despídela, porque viene gritando detrás de nosotros».
es.B: Sus discípulos se acercaron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} insistían: «Despídela, porque no deja de gritar detrás de nosotros».
es.R: Sus seguidores se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaron: «¡Despídela! No deja de seguirnos y de gritar».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, s’étant approchés, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} priaient, disant : « Renvoie-la, car elle crie derrière nous. »
fr.B: Ses disciples vinrent {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} presser : « Renvoie-la, car elle ne cesse de crier derrière nous. »
fr.R: Ses disciples sont venus {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplier : « Renvoie-la ! Elle n’arrête pas de nous suivre en criant. »

sw.L: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimkaribia, wakawa wakimsihi, wakisema, "Mruhusu aondoke, maana analia kwa sauti nyuma yetu."
sw.B: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimjia, wakamsihi tena na tena, "Mwambie aondoke, kwa sababu anaendelea kupiga kelele nyuma yetu."
sw.R: Wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimjia, wakamwomba sana, "Mwambie aende zake! Anaendelea kutufuata huku akipiga kelele."

decisions.choice: send her away: get rid of her, perhaps by giving her what she asks
decisions.reason: The verb means to release or dismiss. The disciples may want her sent off with nothing, or want Jesus to grant her request so she will go. Jesus's answer in 15:24 fits either.

decisions.choice: were urging: they kept on asking
decisions.reason: The tense shows repeated asking.

decisions.choice: les disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers"; French "disciple" is a common, transparent word, and the style guide keeps "les disciples" at every level, as in Mark's French. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: a span on wake (his); none on the object prefix -m- (wakamsihi)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the object prefix -m- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake, yake, nami, kwake). Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἀπεστάλην εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ.

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said, Not I was sent except to the sheep the being lost of house of Israel.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "I was not sent except to the lost sheep of [the] house of Israel."
en.B: He answered, "I was sent only to the lost sheep, the people of Israel."
en.R: Jesus answered, "God sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} only to the people of Israel. They are like sheep that are lost."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, dijo: «No fui enviado sino a las ovejas perdidas de [la] casa de Israel».
es.B: Él respondió: «Solo fui enviado a las ovejas perdidas, al pueblo de Israel».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Dios {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} envió solamente al pueblo de Israel. Ellos son como ovejas perdidas».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répondit et dit : « Je n’ai été envoyé que vers les brebis perdues de la maison d’Israël. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « J’ai été envoyé seulement vers les brebis perdues, le peuple d’Israël. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Dieu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a envoyé seulement vers le peuple d’Israël. Ces gens sont comme des moutons perdus. »

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akajibu, akasema, "Sikutumwa isipokuwa kwa kondoo waliopotea wa nyumba ya Israeli."
sw.B: Alijibu, "Nimetumwa kwa kondoo waliopotea tu, yaani watu wa Israeli."
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Mungu alinituma kwa watu wa Israeli peke yao. Wao ni kama kondoo waliopotea."

decisions.choice: the lost sheep of the house of Israel: the words of 10:6
alternatives: only the lost ones within Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus sent the twelve to the same people (10:6). The whole nation is the lost flock (9:36). The wording is kept the same as in 10:6 at each level.

decisions.choice: I was sent: sent by God
alternatives: I came of my own accord
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the sender unnamed, and the sender is God (10:40).

decisions.choice: a limit for Jesus's earthly mission, not for all time
alternatives: a rule that God cares only for Israel
decisions.reason: Jesus comes first to Israel. After his resurrection he sends his disciples to all nations (28:19).

decisions.choice: God sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names the sender.

source.text: ἡ δὲ ἐλθοῦσα προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγουσα· Κύριε, βοήθει μοι.

records.literal_gloss: She but having come was kneeling to him saying, Lord, help me.

en.L: But she came and knelt before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, help me."
en.B: But she came and bowed low before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "Lord," she said, "help me!"
en.R: Then the woman came and bowed down in front of Jesus. She said, "Lord, help me!"

es.L: Pero ella, viniendo, se postraba ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, diciendo: «Señor, ayúdame».
es.B: Pero ella se acercó y se inclinó hasta el suelo delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. «Señor —le dijo—, ¡ayúdame!».
es.R: Entonces la mujer se acercó y se inclinó delante de Jesús. Le dijo: «¡Señor, ayúdame!».

fr.L: Mais elle vint et se prosterna devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, disant : « Seigneur, viens à mon secours. »
fr.B: Mais elle vint s’incliner jusqu’à terre devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. « Seigneur, dit-elle, aide-moi ! »
fr.R: Alors la femme est venue s’incliner jusqu’à terre devant Jésus. Elle a dit : « Seigneur, aide-moi ! »

sw.L: Lakini yeye, alipofika, alikuwa akipiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akisema, "Bwana, nisaidie."
sw.B: Lakini yule mwanamke alikuja, akainama chini mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Akasema, "Bwana, nisaidie!"
sw.R: Kisha yule mwanamke alikuja, akainama mbele ya Yesu. Akasema, "Bwana, nisaidie!"

decisions.choice: knelt before him: bowed low in honor and appeal
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 2:11, 8:2 and 9:18. Here it is the bow of one asking a great favor, though Matthew's readers hear more in it (14:33).

decisions.choice: help me: her plea for her daughter
decisions.reason: She asks help for herself, since her daughter's suffering is hers too.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔστιν καλὸν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ βαλεῖν τοῖς κυναρίοις.

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said, Not it is good to take the bread of the children and to throw [it] to the little dogs.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw [it] to the little dogs."
en.B: He replied, "It is not good to take bread away from the children and toss it to the little dogs."
en.R: Jesus answered, "It is not right to take the children's food and throw it to the pet dogs."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, dijo: «No es bueno tomar el pan de los niños y arrojar[lo] a los perritos».
es.B: Él le contestó: «No está bien quitarles el pan a los niños para tirárselo a los perritos».
es.R: Jesús le respondió: «No está bien quitarles la comida a los niños y dársela a los perros de la casa».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} répondit et dit : « Il n’est pas bien de prendre le pain des enfants et de [le] jeter aux petits chiens. »
fr.B: Il répondit : « Il n’est pas bon d’enlever le pain aux enfants pour le lancer aux petits chiens. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Ce n’est pas bien de prendre la nourriture des enfants pour la jeter aux chiens de la maison. »

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akajibu, akasema, "Si jambo jema kuchukua mkate wa watoto na kuwatupia mbwa wadogo."
sw.B: Alimjibu, "Haifai kuwanyang'anya watoto mkate wao na kuwarushia mbwa wadogo."
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Si sawa kuchukua chakula cha watoto na kuwatupia mbwa wa nyumbani."

decisions.choice: little dogs: house dogs kept indoors
alternatives: dogs in general, with no softening
decisions.reason: The word is a small form of the word for dog and fits dogs under a family table (15:27). Small forms often lost their force in the Greek of this time, so the word may simply mean dogs. And "dogs" was a name some Jews used for Gentiles, so the saying is still a hard one.

decisions.choice: the children: Israel; the dogs: the Gentiles
alternatives: a general proverb with no reference
decisions.reason: The saying applies 15:24 in a picture. The children of the household are fed first.

decisions.choice: it is not right: it is not fitting, like a household rule
decisions.reason: The word speaks of what is proper.

decisions.choice: food; pet dogs
decisions.reason: Readable shows that these are dogs living in the house, as in Mark 7:27, and says that bread here means food.

decisions.choice: perritos (L, B); perros de la casa (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the small form of "dog", probably the house dogs kept indoors (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Perritos" keeps the small form; Readable says where they live, as the English "pet dogs" does. The same in verse 27.

decisions.choice: mbwa wadogo (L, B); mbwa wa nyumbani (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the small form of "dog", probably the house dogs kept indoors (meaning decision m1, uncertain). "Mbwa wadogo" keeps the small form without the contempt the diminutive "vibwa" can carry; Readable says where they live, as the English "pet dogs" does. The same in verse 27.

source.text: ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, κύριε, καὶ γὰρ τὰ κυνάρια ἐσθίει ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τῶν κυρίων αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: She but said, Yes, Lord, even for the little dogs eat from the crumbs the falling from the table of the masters of them.

en.L: But she said, "Yes, Lord, for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."
en.B: She said, "That is true, Lord. Still, the little dogs eat some of the crumbs that drop from the table where their masters eat."
en.R: She said, "Yes, Lord. But even the pet dogs get to eat the crumbs that fall from the table where their owners eat."

es.L: Pero ella dijo: «Sí, Señor, pues también los perritos comen de las migajas que caen de la mesa de sus señores».
es.B: Ella dijo: «Es verdad, Señor. Pero los perritos comen algo de las migajas que caen de la mesa donde comen sus amos».
es.R: Ella le dijo: «Sí, Señor. Pero hasta los perros de la casa se comen las migajas que caen de la mesa donde comen sus dueños».

fr.L: Mais elle dit : « Oui, Seigneur, car même les petits chiens mangent des miettes qui tombent de la table de leurs maîtres. »
fr.B: Elle dit : « C’est vrai, Seigneur. Pourtant, les petits chiens mangent bien quelques miettes qui tombent de la table où mangent leurs maîtres. »
fr.R: Elle a dit : « Oui, Seigneur. Mais même les chiens de la maison peuvent manger les miettes qui tombent de la table où mangent leurs propriétaires. »

sw.L: Lakini yeye akasema, "Naam, Bwana, kwa kuwa hata mbwa wadogo hula sehemu ya chembe zinazodondoka kutoka kwenye meza ya mabwana zao."
sw.B: Akasema, "Ni kweli, Bwana. Hata hivyo, mbwa wadogo hula baadhi ya chembe zinazodondoka kutoka mezani wanapokula mabwana zao."
sw.R: Akasema, "Ndiyo, Bwana. Lakini hata mbwa wa nyumbani hupata kula vipande vidogo vinavyoanguka kutoka mezani wanapokula wamiliki wao."

decisions.choice: yes ... for even: she accepts his picture and finds room in it for herself
decisions.reason: She agrees that the children come first. The dogs, she says, are fed in the same house at the same meal, from what falls.

decisions.choice: masters: the owners of the house, the same word as "Lord"
decisions.reason: She calls Jesus Lord and speaks of the dogs' masters with the same word. The point is that the dogs belong to the household.

decisions.choice: Still (B); But even (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show how her reply turns his saying.

decisions.choice: owners
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word for the people a dog belongs to.

decisions.choice: sus señores (L); sus amos (B); sus dueños (R)
decisions.reason: The word for the dogs' masters is the same word she uses for Jesus, "Lord" (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "señores" so the link shows; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary words for owners of animals.

decisions.choice: mabwana zao (their masters)
decisions.reason: The word for the dogs' masters is the same word she uses for Jesus, "Lord" (meaning decision m2). Swahili "bwana" can carry both, so Literal and Balanced keep the link; Readable says "wamiliki" (owners), as the English does.

source.text: τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Ὦ γύναι, μεγάλη σου ἡ πίστις· γενηθήτω σοι ὡς θέλεις.

records.literal_gloss: Then answering the Jesus said to her, O woman, great of you the faith; let it be to you as you wish.

en.L: Then Jesus answered and said to her, "O woman, great [is] your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish."
en.B: Then Jesus told her, "Woman, your faith is great. May it be done for you as you wish."
en.R: Then Jesus answered her, "Woman, your faith is very great! What you asked for will happen."

es.L: Entonces Jesús, respondiendo, le dijo: «¡Oh mujer, grande [es] tu fe! Sea para ti como deseas».
es.B: Entonces Jesús le dijo: «Mujer, tu fe es grande. Que se cumpla lo que deseas».
es.R: Entonces Jesús le respondió: «Mujer, ¡qué grande es tu fe! Lo que pediste va a suceder».

fr.L: Alors Jésus répondit et lui dit : « Ô femme, grande [est] ta foi ! Qu’il te soit fait comme tu veux. »
fr.B: Alors Jésus lui dit : « Femme, ta foi est grande. Qu’il te soit fait comme tu le désires. »
fr.R: Alors Jésus lui a répondu : « Femme, ta foi est très grande ! Ce que tu as demandé va se réaliser. »

sw.L: Kisha Yesu, akijibu, akamwambia, "Ee Mama, kubwa [ni] imani yako! Na ufanyiwe kama unavyotaka."
sw.B: Kisha Yesu alimwambia, "Mama, una imani kubwa. Ufanyiwe kama unavyotaka."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alimjibu, "Mama, imani yako ni kubwa sana! Ulichoomba kitatokea."

decisions.choice: faith: her trust in Jesus's power and mercy
alternatives: her belief in a set of teachings
decisions.reason: She kept asking, even when refused. Matthew praises the faith of a Gentile, as with the centurion (8:10), while the disciples have "little faith" (14:31).

decisions.choice: O woman: a strong, respectful address
decisions.reason: The added word gives feeling to the address. "Woman" was a polite way to speak to a woman.

decisions.choice: let it be done: Jesus's word grants the healing
decisions.reason: As in 8:13, Jesus heals at a distance by his word.

decisions.choice: Mama
decisions.reason: As in John 2:4: a man calling a woman "Mwanamke!" to her face is rude in Swahili, while "Mama" is the respectful address to a woman. The Greek is a strong, respectful address (meaning decision m2), so "Mama" at every level.

source.text: καὶ ἰάθη ἡ θυγάτηρ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.

records.literal_gloss: And was healed the daughter of her from the hour that.

en.L: And her daughter was healed from that hour.
en.B: And from that moment her daughter was well.
en.R: Her daughter was healed at that very moment.

es.L: Y quedó sana su hija desde aquella hora.
es.B: Y desde aquel momento su hija quedó bien.
es.R: Su hija se sanó en ese mismo momento.

fr.L: Et sa fille fut guérie dès cette heure-là.
fr.B: Et dès ce moment, sa fille fut rétablie.
fr.R: Sa fille a été guérie au moment même.

sw.L: Na binti yake akaponywa tangu saa ile.
sw.B: Na tangu wakati ule binti yake alikuwa mzima.
sw.R: Binti yake alipona wakati huo huo.

decisions.choice: from that hour: at the moment Jesus spoke
decisions.reason: As in 8:13 and 9:22. The healing came at once, without Jesus going to the girl.

source.text: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἀναβὰς εἰς τὸ ὄρος ἐκάθητο ἐκεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And having moved on from there the Jesus came beside the sea of the Galilee, and having gone up into the mountain he was sitting there.

en.L: And moving on from there, Jesus came beside the Sea of Galilee, and going up onto the mountain, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down there.
en.B: From there Jesus moved on and came along the shore of the Sea of Galilee. He went up onto the mountain and sat down there.
en.R: Jesus went on from there and walked along the shore of Lake Galilee. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up on a hill and sat down.

es.L: Y pasando de allí, Jesús vino junto al mar de Galilea, y subiendo al monte, se sentó allí.
es.B: De allí Jesús siguió adelante y fue por la orilla del mar de Galilea. Subió al monte y se sentó allí.
es.R: Jesús se fue de allí y caminó por la orilla del lago de Galilea. Luego subió a un cerro y se sentó.

fr.L: Et partant de là, Jésus vint près de la mer de Galilée ; et étant monté sur la montagne, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’y assit.
fr.B: De là, Jésus poursuivit sa route et longea la mer de Galilée. Il monta sur la montagne et s’y assit.
fr.R: Jésus est parti de là et a marché le long du lac de Galilée. Ensuite, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est monté sur une colline et s’est assis.

sw.L: Na alipoondoka huko, Yesu alikuja kando ya Bahari ya Galilaya, na alipopanda mlimani, alikuwa ameketi huko.
sw.B: Kutoka hapo Yesu aliendelea, akafika kando ya Bahari ya Galilaya. Akapanda mlimani, akaketi huko.
sw.R: Yesu aliondoka pale, akatembea kando ya Ziwa Galilaya. Kisha akapanda kilimani, akaketi.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Galilee: the large freshwater lake
decisions.reason: As in 4:18. The lake is called a sea.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hills by the lake, not named
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "the mountain", as in 5:1 and 14:23.

decisions.choice: sat down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: As in 5:1, Jewish teachers sat to teach. Here the crowds come to him there.

decisions.choice: Lake Galilee
decisions.reason: As in 4:18, Readable says it is a lake.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on "se sentó"
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Spanish leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb, where there is nothing separate to capitalise, so the setting covers only separate pronouns and possessives (él, le, lo, me, sus). Spanish therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

source.text: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἔχοντες μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν κωφούς, τυφλούς, χωλούς, κυλλούς, καὶ ἑτέρους πολλούς, καὶ ἔρριψαν αὐτοὺς παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: And came to him crowds great having with themselves mute, blind, lame, crippled, and others many, and they threw them at the feet of him, and he healed them;

en.L: And great crowds came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having with them [the] mute, blind, lame, crippled, and many others, and they laid them at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.
en.B: Large crowds came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, bringing people who could not speak, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others. They laid them down at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.
en.R: Large crowds of people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They brought people who could not talk, people who were blind, people who could not walk, people whose arms or legs were damaged, and many others. They put them down in front of Jesus, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed them.

es.L: Y se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron grandes multitudes, que tenían consigo mudos, ciegos, cojos, lisiados y otros muchos, y los echaron a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, y los sanó.
es.B: Grandes multitudes se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron, trayendo a personas que no podían hablar, a ciegos, cojos, lisiados y a muchos otros. Los pusieron a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los sanó.
es.R: Grandes multitudes de gente se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} acercaron. Traían a personas que no podían hablar, a personas ciegas, a personas que no podían caminar, a personas con los brazos o las piernas lisiados, y a muchos otros. Los pusieron delante de Jesús, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los sanó.

fr.L: Et de grandes foules vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ayant avec elles des muets, des aveugles, des boiteux, des estropiés, et beaucoup d’autres, et ils les déposèrent à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit.
fr.B: De grandes foules vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, amenant des gens qui ne pouvaient pas parler, des aveugles, des boiteux, des estropiés et beaucoup d’autres. On les déposa à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les guérit.
fr.R: De grandes foules sont venues vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Les gens amenaient des personnes qui ne pouvaient pas parler, des aveugles, des personnes qui ne pouvaient pas marcher, des personnes qui avaient un bras ou une jambe infirme, et beaucoup d’autres. Ils les ont posées devant Jésus, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a guéries.

sw.L: Na umati mkubwa wa watu ukamjia, wakiwa na bubu, vipofu, viwete, vilema, na wengine wengi, wakawalaza chini ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, naye akawaponya.
sw.B: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulimjia, ukiwaleta watu wasioweza kusema, vipofu, viwete, vilema na wengine wengi. Wakawalaza chini ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, naye akawaponya.
sw.R: Umati mkubwa wa watu ulimjia. Walileta watu wasioweza kuzungumza, watu wasioona, watu wasioweza kutembea, watu ambao mikono au miguu yao ilikuwa imelemaa, na wengine wengi. Wakawaweka chini mbele ya Yesu, naye akawaponya.

decisions.choice: mute: unable to speak
decisions.reason: The word can mean deaf or mute (11:5). In 15:31 they are seen speaking, so the mute are meant.

decisions.choice: crippled: with a hand or limb deformed or maimed
decisions.reason: The word is different from "lame" and describes a twisted or damaged limb.

decisions.choice: laid them: put them down in haste
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or cast. It shows how eager the crowds were, not that the sick were handled roughly.

decisions.choice: mute, blind, lame, crippled, the order of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the same four in other orders
decisions.reason: Manuscripts give the list in several orders. The meaning is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

decisions.choice: ils les déposèrent
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is "throw", but here it means putting the sick down in haste (m3); French "jeter" would say that they were thrown, so Literal says "déposer", as Balanced does.

source.text: ὥστε τὸν ὄχλον θαυμάσαι βλέποντας κωφοὺς λαλοῦντας κυλλοὺς ὑγιεῖς καὶ χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας καὶ τυφλοὺς βλέποντας· καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν θεὸν Ἰσραήλ.

records.literal_gloss: So that the crowd marveled seeing mute speaking, crippled whole, and lame walking, and blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

en.L: So the crowd marveled, seeing [the] mute speaking, [the] crippled whole, and [the] lame walking, and [the] blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.
en.B: The crowd was amazed to see the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking and the blind able to see. And they glorified the God of Israel.
en.R: The people were amazed. Those who could not talk were talking. People whose arms or legs were damaged were well again. People who could not walk were walking, and blind people could see. And the crowd gave glory to the God of Israel.

es.L: De modo que la multitud se maravilló al ver a mudos hablando, lisiados sanos, y cojos andando, y ciegos viendo; y glorificaron al Dios de Israel.
es.B: La multitud se asombraba al ver que los mudos hablaban, los lisiados quedaban sanos, los cojos andaban y los ciegos veían. Y glorificaron al Dios de Israel.
es.R: La gente estaba asombrada. Los que no podían hablar estaban hablando. Los que tenían los brazos o las piernas lisiados estaban sanos otra vez. Los que no podían caminar caminaban, y los ciegos veían. Y la multitud dio gloria al Dios de Israel.

fr.L: De sorte que la foule s’émerveilla en voyant des muets parler, des estropiés guéris, des boiteux marcher et des aveugles voir ; et ils glorifièrent le Dieu d’Israël.
fr.B: La foule fut dans l’étonnement en voyant les muets parler, les estropiés guéris, les boiteux marcher et les aveugles voir. Et ils glorifièrent le Dieu d’Israël.
fr.R: Les gens étaient étonnés. Ceux qui ne pouvaient pas parler parlaient. Ceux qui avaient un bras ou une jambe infirme étaient guéris. Ceux qui ne pouvaient pas marcher marchaient, et les aveugles voyaient. Et la foule a rendu gloire au Dieu d’Israël.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo umati ulishangaa, ukiona bubu wakiongea, vilema wakiwa wamepona, viwete wakitembea, na vipofu wakiona; nao wakamtukuza Mungu wa Israeli.
sw.B: Umati ulishangaa kuona bubu wakizungumza, vilema wakifanywa wazima, viwete wakitembea na vipofu wakiweza kuona. Nao wakamtukuza Mungu wa Israeli.
sw.R: Watu walishangaa. Wale wasioweza kuzungumza walikuwa wakizungumza. Wale ambao mikono au miguu yao ilikuwa imelemaa walikuwa wazima tena. Wale wasioweza kutembea walikuwa wakitembea, na vipofu waliona. Nao umati ukampa utukufu Mungu wa Israeli.

decisions.choice: the God of Israel: perhaps praise from Gentiles, perhaps a Jewish form of praise
alternatives: a phrase with no special meaning here
decisions.reason: The words may mean that the crowd was largely Gentile, praising Israel's God; Mark 7:31 places a healing at this time in the Ten Towns. But the phrase is also a Jewish form of praise (Psalm 41:13; Luke 1:68), and Matthew does not say who the crowd were.

decisions.choice: the mute speak, the lame walk, the blind see: Isaiah 35:5-6
alternatives: a simple report with no background
decisions.reason: As in 11:5, these are the signs Isaiah promised for the time when God comes to save.

decisions.choice: the crippled whole, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: no mention of the crippled, in some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "the crippled whole". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: glorified: praised God and gave him honor
decisions.reason: As in 9:8, the crowd gives God the honor for what he has done.

decisions.choice: gave glory to
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term in a simpler phrase, as in 9:8.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν· Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον, ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν· καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτοὺς νήστεις οὐ θέλω, μήποτε ἐκλυθῶσιν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.

records.literal_gloss: The and Jesus having called to [him] the disciples of him said, I have compassion on the crowd, because already days three they remain with me and not they have anything they may eat; and to send away them hungry not I am willing, lest they faint on the way.

en.L: And Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and said, "I have compassion on the crowd, because already for three days they remain with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they do not have anything to eat; and I am not willing to send them away hungry, lest they faint on the way."
en.B: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples together and said, "I feel deep pity for the crowd. For three days now they have stayed with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they have nothing left to eat. If I send them off without food, they may give out on the way, and I am not willing to do that."
en.R: Jesus called {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "I feel sorry for these people. They have been here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} for three days, and now they have nothing to eat. If I send them home hungry, they may become weak and faint on the road. I do not want that."

es.L: Y Jesús, llamando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, dijo: «Siento compasión por la multitud, porque ya llevan tres días quedándose conmigo y no tienen nada que comer; y no quiero despedirlos hambrientos, no sea que se desmayen por el camino».
es.B: Jesús llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dijo: «Siento una profunda lástima por esta multitud. Ya llevan tres días conmigo y no les queda nada que comer. Si los despido sin comer, pueden desfallecer por el camino, y no quiero hacer eso».
es.R: Jesús llamó a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores y les dijo: «Me da pena esta gente. Llevan tres días aquí conmigo, y ahora no tienen nada que comer. Si los mando a casa con hambre, pueden debilitarse y desmayarse en el camino. No quiero que pase eso».

fr.L: Et Jésus, ayant appelé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, dit : « J’ai compassion de la foule, car voilà déjà trois jours qu’ils restent avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et ils n’ont pas de quoi manger ; et je ne veux pas les renvoyer à jeun, de peur qu’ils ne défaillent en chemin. »
fr.B: Jésus appela {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et dit : « Je suis pris de pitié pour cette foule. Voilà trois jours déjà qu’ils sont avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et ils n’ont plus rien à manger. Si je les renvoie sans nourriture, ils risquent de s’effondrer en route, et cela, je ne le veux pas. »
fr.R: Jésus a appelé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il leur a dit : « J’ai pitié de ces gens. Ils sont ici avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} depuis trois jours, et maintenant ils n’ont plus rien à manger. Si je les renvoie chez eux le ventre vide, ils vont se sentir faibles et s’évanouir en chemin. Je ne veux pas cela. »

sw.L: Na Yesu, akiisha kuwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, alisema, "Moyo wangu unauonea huruma umati huu, kwa kuwa sasa ni siku tatu wamebaki {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, nao hawana chochote cha kula. Na sitaki kuwaruhusu waondoke na njaa, wasije wakaishiwa nguvu njiani."
sw.B: Yesu aliwaita wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akasema, "Ninawaonea huruma sana watu hawa. Sasa ni siku tatu wamekaa {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}}, na hawana chakula kilichobaki. Nikiwaruhusu waende bila kula, wanaweza kuishiwa nguvu njiani, na sitaki kufanya hivyo."
sw.R: Yesu aliwaita wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Akasema, "Ninawasikitikia watu hawa. Wamekuwa hapa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} kwa siku tatu, na sasa hawana chochote cha kula. Nikiwaaga waende nyumbani wakiwa na njaa, wanaweza kuchoka na kuzimia njiani. Sitaki hilo litokee."

decisions.choice: have compassion: be moved deep within with pity
decisions.reason: As in 9:36 and 14:14. The verb comes from the word for the inner parts, thought of as the seat of feeling.

decisions.choice: already three days: they have stayed so long that their food is gone
decisions.reason: The point is how long they have stayed with Jesus in a place far from towns.

decisions.choice: faint: give out from hunger and weakness
decisions.reason: The verb means to become weak or collapse.

decisions.choice: feel deep pity
decisions.reason: As in 9:36.

decisions.choice: the condition first, then Jesus's refusal
alternatives: I am not willing to send them away hungry, lest they faint
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the danger first and ends on Jesus's resolve.

decisions.choice: moyo wangu unauonea huruma (my heart feels pity for)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is pity felt deep within (meaning decision m1). Literal names the heart to keep that depth; Balanced says "ninawaonea huruma sana".

source.text: καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί· Πόθεν ἡμῖν ἐν ἐρημίᾳ ἄρτοι τοσοῦτοι ὥστε χορτάσαι ὄχλον τοσοῦτον;

records.literal_gloss: And say to him the disciples, From where to us in a desolate place loaves so many as to satisfy a crowd so great?

en.L: And the disciples say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where [are we to get] so many loaves in a desolate place to satisfy so great a crowd?"
en.B: The disciples said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Here in this lonely place, where could we find enough bread to feed such a crowd?"
en.R: His followers answered, "We are far away from any town. Where can we get enough bread to feed all these people?"

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen los discípulos: «¿De dónde [sacaríamos] nosotros en un desierto tantos panes como para saciar a una multitud tan grande?».
es.B: Los discípulos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Aquí, en este lugar despoblado, ¿dónde podríamos conseguir pan suficiente para alimentar a tanta gente?».
es.R: Sus seguidores {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondieron: «Estamos lejos de cualquier pueblo. ¿Dónde vamos a conseguir pan suficiente para dar de comer a toda esta gente?».

fr.L: Et les disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « D’où [prendrions]-nous, dans un lieu désert, assez de pains pour rassasier une si grande foule ? »
fr.B: Les disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dirent : « Ici, dans ce lieu désert, où pourrions-nous trouver assez de pain pour nourrir une telle foule ? »
fr.R: Ses disciples {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont répondu : « Nous sommes loin de toute ville. Où pouvons-nous trouver assez de pain pour nourrir tous ces gens ? »

sw.L: Na wanafunzi wanamwambia, "Wapi [tutapata] sisi nyikani mikate mingi hivi, ili kushibisha umati mkubwa hivi?"
sw.B: Wanafunzi walimwambia, "Hapa mahali hapa pasipo na watu, tungeweza kupata wapi mkate wa kutosha kulisha umati mkubwa kiasi hiki?"
sw.R: Wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walijibu, "Tuko mbali na mji wowote. Tutapata wapi mkate wa kutosha kuwalisha watu wote hawa?"

decisions.choice: a desolate place: open country, far from towns
decisions.reason: As in 14:15, the word means land with few people, not a desert of sand.

decisions.choice: the disciples' question after the feeding of 14:13-21
alternatives: a request that Jesus feed them again
decisions.reason: Matthew does not explain why they ask this after the first feeding. In 16:9-10 Jesus reminds them of both feedings.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: We are far away from any town
decisions.reason: Readable says what the place was like.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dicen); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (dijeron, respondieron)
decisions.reason: Matthew often tells a past event in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verse 34.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (wanamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable (walimwambia, walijibu)
decisions.reason: Matthew often tells a past event in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past. The same in verse 34.

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πόσους ἄρτους ἔχετε;

records.literal_gloss: And says to them the Jesus, How many loaves have you?

en.L: And Jesus says to them, "How many loaves do you have?"
en.B: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves have you got?"
en.R: Jesus asked them, "How many loaves of bread do you have?"

es.L: Y Jesús les dice: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».
es.B: Jesús les preguntó: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».
es.R: Jesús les preguntó: «¿Cuántos panes {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}?».

fr.L: Et Jésus leur dit : « Combien de pains avez-vous ? »
fr.B: Jésus leur demanda : « Combien de pains avez-vous ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a demandé : « Vous avez combien de pains ? »

sw.L: Na Yesu anawaambia, "Mna mikate mingapi?"
sw.B: Yesu aliwauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"
sw.R: Yesu aliwauliza, "Mna mikate mingapi?"

decisions.choice: loaves: small flat loaves of bread
decisions.reason: A loaf was a small round bread, enough for one person's meal.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" (the default) and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so the span has no English counterpart.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά, καὶ ὀλίγα ἰχθύδια.

records.literal_gloss: They and said, Seven, and a few small fish.

en.L: And they said, "Seven, and a few small fish."
en.B: "Seven," they said, "and a few little fish."
en.R: They said, "Seven loaves, and a few small fish."

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «Siete, y unos pocos pescaditos».
es.B: «Siete —dijeron—, y unos cuantos pescaditos».
es.R: Ellos dijeron: «Siete panes y unos pocos pescados pequeños».

fr.L: Et ils dirent : « Sept, et quelques petits poissons. »
fr.B: « Sept, répondirent-ils, et quelques petits poissons. »
fr.R: Ils ont répondu : « Sept pains, et quelques petits poissons. »

sw.L: Nao wakasema, "Saba, na visamaki vichache."
sw.B: "Saba," wakasema, "na samaki wadogo wachache."
sw.R: Wakasema, "Mikate saba, na samaki wadogo wachache."

decisions.choice: small fish: little fish, probably dried or salted
decisions.reason: The word is a small form of the word for fish. Fish from the lake were often dried or salted and eaten with bread.

source.text: καὶ παραγγείλας τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἔλαβεν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς ἰχθύας καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις.

records.literal_gloss: And having directed the crowd to sit down on the ground \v 36 he took the seven loaves and the fish and having given thanks he broke and was giving to the disciples, the and disciples to the crowds.

en.L: And having directed the crowd to sit down on the ground, \v 36 {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the seven loaves and the fish, and having given thanks, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke [them] and was giving [them] to the disciples, and the disciples [gave them] to the crowds.
en.B: He told the crowd to sit down on the ground. \v 36 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and broke them. He kept handing them to the disciples, and the disciples handed them to the people.
en.R: Jesus told the people to sit down on the ground. \v 36 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took the seven loaves and the fish and thanked God for them. He broke them into pieces and kept giving them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers, and the followers gave them to the people.

es.L: Y habiendo mandado a la multitud que se recostara en el suelo, \v 36 tomó los siete panes y los pescados, y habiendo dado gracias, [los] partió y [los] daba a los discípulos, y los discípulos a las multitudes.
es.B: Mandó a la gente que se sentara en el suelo. \v 36 Luego tomó los siete panes y los pescados, dio gracias y los partió. Se los iba dando a los discípulos, y los discípulos se los daban a la gente.
es.R: Jesús le dijo a la gente que se sentara en el suelo. \v 36 Luego tomó los siete panes y los pescados, y le dio gracias a Dios por ellos. Los partió en pedazos y se los iba dando a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} seguidores, y los seguidores se los daban a la gente.

fr.L: Et ayant ordonné à la foule de s’asseoir par terre, \v 36 {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les sept pains et les poissons, et ayant rendu grâce, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [les] rompit et [les] donnait aux disciples, et les disciples aux foules.
fr.B: Il ordonna à la foule de s’asseoir par terre. \v 36 Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} prit les sept pains et les poissons, rendit grâce et les rompit. Il les donnait au fur et à mesure aux disciples, et les disciples les distribuaient à la foule.
fr.R: Jésus a dit aux gens de s’asseoir par terre. \v 36 Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a pris les sept pains et les poissons, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a remercié Dieu pour cette nourriture. Il l’a partagée en morceaux et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la donnait à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et les disciples la donnaient aux gens.

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kuuagiza umati uketi chini, \v 36 alichukua ile mikate saba na wale samaki, na alipokwisha kushukuru, akaimega, akawa akiwapa wanafunzi, nao wanafunzi [wakawapa] umati.
sw.B: Aliwaambia watu waketi chini. \v 36 Kisha akachukua ile mikate saba na wale samaki, akashukuru, akaimega. Akawa akiwapa wanafunzi, nao wanafunzi wakawagawia watu.
sw.R: Yesu aliwaambia watu waketi chini. \v 36 Kisha akachukua ile mikate saba na wale samaki, akamshukuru Mungu kwa ajili ya chakula hicho. Akavimega vipande vipande, akawa akiwapa wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, nao wafuasi wakawapa watu.

decisions.choice: took, gave thanks, broke, gave: the actions of the first feeding and the Last Supper
decisions.reason: The same series comes at the first feeding (14:19) and at the Last Supper, where the verb for giving thanks is used of the cup (26:26-27).

decisions.choice: gave thanks: thanked God, as at the start of a Jewish meal
decisions.reason: At meals a Jew gave thanks to God for the food. At 14:19 Matthew says "blessed"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: was giving: he kept handing out the food
decisions.reason: The tense describes repeated action as the bread kept coming.

decisions.choice: thanked God for them
decisions.reason: Readable names God, to whom the thanks were given.

source.text: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων ἦραν ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας πλήρεις.

records.literal_gloss: And ate all and were satisfied, and the remaining of the broken pieces they took up seven large baskets full.

en.L: And they all ate and were satisfied, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven large baskets full.
en.B: Everyone ate until they were full. Then they gathered up the leftover pieces, and these filled seven large baskets.
en.R: All the people ate as much as they wanted. Then they picked up the pieces of food that were left. They filled seven big baskets.

es.L: Y comieron todos y quedaron satisfechos, y lo sobrante de los trozos recogieron: siete grandes cestos llenos.
es.B: Todos comieron hasta quedar satisfechos. Después recogieron los trozos que sobraron, y llenaron siete cestos grandes.
es.R: Toda la gente comió todo lo que quiso. Después recogieron los pedazos de comida que sobraron. Llenaron siete canastos grandes.

fr.L: Et tous mangèrent et furent rassasiés, et ils ramassèrent ce qui restait des morceaux : sept grandes corbeilles pleines.
fr.B: Tous mangèrent à leur faim. Puis on ramassa les morceaux qui restaient, et ils remplirent sept grandes corbeilles.
fr.R: Tous les gens ont mangé autant qu’ils voulaient. Ensuite, on a ramassé les morceaux qui restaient. Ils ont rempli sept grandes corbeilles.

sw.L: Na wote walikula, wakashiba, na mabaki ya vipande wakaokota, vikapu vikubwa saba vilivyojaa.
sw.B: Wote walikula mpaka wakashiba. Kisha wakakusanya vipande vilivyobaki, navyo vikajaa vikapu vikubwa saba.
sw.R: Watu wote walikula kadiri walivyotaka. Kisha wakaokota vipande vya chakula vilivyobaki. Wakajaza vikapu vikubwa saba.

decisions.choice: large baskets: big woven baskets or hampers
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the basket of 14:20. It names a larger basket, big enough to let a man down over a wall (Acts 9:25). Jesus keeps the two words apart in 16:9-10.

decisions.choice: were satisfied: were fed until full
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 14:20 and 15:33.

decisions.choice: large baskets (L, B); big baskets (R)
decisions.reason: The size is part of the meaning of the word. Every level marks it so that readers can tell these baskets from those of 14:20, as in Mark 8:8.

decisions.choice: grandes corbeilles (15:37, 16:10); paniers (14:20, 16:9)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 8:8: Matthew uses two different words for the baskets of the two feedings, and French keeps two different words, "grandes corbeilles" for the large hampers here and "paniers" for the ordinary baskets of 14:20.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν τετρακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων.

records.literal_gloss: Those and eating were four thousand men apart from women and children.

en.L: And those who ate were 4,000 men, apart from women and children.
en.B: Those who ate numbered 4,000 men, and there were women and children besides.
en.R: There were 4,000 men who ate, and there were also women and children.

es.L: Y los que comieron eran 4000 hombres, sin contar mujeres y niños.
es.B: Los que comieron eran 4000 hombres, además de las mujeres y los niños.
es.R: Comieron 4000 hombres, y también había mujeres y niños.

fr.L: Or ceux qui mangeaient étaient quatre mille hommes, sans compter les femmes et les enfants.
fr.B: Ceux qui avaient mangé étaient au nombre de quatre mille hommes, sans compter les femmes et les enfants.
fr.R: Il y avait quatre mille hommes qui avaient mangé, et il y avait aussi des femmes et des enfants.

sw.L: Basi wale waliokuwa wakila walikuwa wanaume elfu nne, mbali na wanawake na watoto.
sw.B: Wale waliokula walikuwa wanaume elfu nne, na zaidi ya hao walikuwepo wanawake na watoto.
sw.R: Wanaume waliokula walikuwa elfu nne, na pia walikuwepo wanawake na watoto.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word means men, not people in general, and Matthew adds that women and children were also there, as in 14:21. Mark 8:9 simply counts about 4,000.

decisions.choice: counting the men: a common way of counting a crowd
decisions.reason: Crowds were often counted by the men. Matthew makes clear that the whole crowd was larger.

decisions.choice: men, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Here the word means males, as the mention of women and children shows, so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: quatre mille, in words
decisions.reason: As in Mark 8:9: the English writes 4,000 in figures; French Bibles usually write round numbers like these in words, which read better aloud. "Hommes" takes no gender setting, as the English decision says.

source.text: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἐνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Μαγαδάν.

records.literal_gloss: And having sent away the crowds he got into the boat, and came into the region of Magadan.

en.L: And sending away the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat and came into the region of Magadan.
en.B: After sending the crowds away, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.
en.R: Then Jesus sent the people home. He got into the boat and went to the area of Magadan.

es.L: Y despidiendo a las multitudes, subió a la barca y vino a la región de Magadán.
es.B: Después de despedir a la gente, subió a la barca y se fue a la región de Magadán.
es.R: Luego Jesús despidió a la gente. Subió a la barca y se fue a la zona de Magadán.

fr.L: Et ayant renvoyé les foules, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans la barque et vint dans le territoire de Magadan.
fr.B: Après avoir renvoyé les foules, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans la barque et se rendit dans la région de Magadan.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus a renvoyé les gens chez eux. Il est monté dans la barque et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est allé dans la région de Magadan.

sw.L: Na alipokwisha kuuaga umati, aliingia katika mashua, akaja pande za Magadani.
sw.B: Baada ya kuuaga umati, aliingia katika mashua, akaenda eneo la Magadani.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwaaga watu warudi nyumbani. Akaingia katika mashua, akaenda sehemu ya Magadani.

decisions.choice: Magadan, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Magdala, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read Magdala, the known town on the west shore of the lake, the home of Mary Magdalene. Scribes probably replaced an unknown name with a known one. Mark 8:10 has Dalmanutha. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Magadan: a place by the lake not known from any other source
decisions.reason: Where Magadan lay is not known. Pharisees and Sadducees meet Jesus there next (16:1), which suggests Jewish territory on the west side of the lake.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.
